title: Pay partner refunds to the cent

blocks.text: A marketplace pays out the refunds its partners report. The partner feed gives each amount in euros as a `double`, and the bank wants whole cents. Customers complain that some refunds arrive a cent short, reversals sometimes take back a cent too little, and last month a partner's broken export produced a batch of payouts for 0 cents that nobody noticed until the customers called.

`RefundBatch.payouts` already builds the instructions. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/RefundBatch.java`: `toCents(euros)` returns the amount the feed means, to the nearest cent, for positive and negative amounts alike, and stops the batch with an `IllegalArgumentException` when the amount isn't a usable number.

cases.says: amounts that are whole euros, halves or quarters become the same number of cents
an amount such as 1.15, whose product with 100 lands just below the whole cent, is paid in full
a negative amount such as -1.15 takes back the full amount, rounded to the nearest cent
a NaN or infinite amount stops the batch with an IllegalArgumentException instead of becoming a payout

origin.section: Casting a double to int or long Truncates Toward Zero, Clamps at the Range, and Turns NaN Into 0

concepts: Casting a double to an integer type truncates toward zero, so a computed amount just below a whole number loses one; Math.round rounds to nearest, and adding 0.5 before the cast is wrong for negative values.
A cast from NaN gives 0 and Math.round(NaN) is 0, so a value that is not a number becomes a plausible zero unless the code rejects it.
